title: The Mystery of the Invisible Bugs
text: Have you ever wondered why superhero kids rarely get sick? Imagine a sneaky, invisible army trying to sneak into your castle. How do we stop them?

title: What do you think?
text: If your hands look clean after playing in the mud, do you think they are really clean? What would happen if we looked at them with a magic magnifying glass?

content.title: The Magic Magnifying Glass
content.description: Looking closely at a 'clean' hand to see the hidden germs.

title: Meet the Germs!
text: Those invisible bugs are called **Germs**. Soap is like our superhero shield! When we wash our hands, brush our teeth, and take a bath, we wash the germs away.

content.definition: Tiny invisible living things that can make you sick if they get inside your body.
Keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy and stop germs from spreading.

content.question: What is the best way to get rid of germs on your hands?
options: Washing them with soap and water

content.tip: Sing the 'Happy Birthday' song twice while washing your hands. That's exactly how long it takes to wash all the germs away!

content.mistake: Thinking hands are clean just because they don't look dirty.
content.correction: Germs are too small to see! Always use soap, especially before eating and after using the toilet.

content.title: Reflection Time
content.description: Close your eyes and think: When are the 3 most important times you should wash your hands every day? Tell your partner!

title: Connecting the Dots
text: Just like a car needs to be washed to look good, and needs good fuel to run fast, your body needs to be clean on the outside AND needs healthy food on the inside!

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Healthy Ninja
content.description: For the next 24 hours, track how many times you wash your hands, brush your teeth (morning and night!), and take a bath. Can you get a perfect score?

title: The Engine of Your Body
text: Have you ever seen a toy car slow down when its battery is low? What happens to you when you don't eat or sleep?

title: Food for Thought
text: If you ate only chocolates all day, would you become super strong or super tired?

content.title: The Energy Battery
content.description: How healthy food and sleep charge our body's battery.

title: Fueling Up!
text: **Healthy Food** like fruits and vegetables give us energy to play. **Sleep** (at least 10 hours for kids!) is when our body grows and repairs itself. **Exercise** makes our muscles strong!

content.definition: Moving your body to make it strong and fit, like running, jumping, or playing sports.

content.question: Which of these is a healthy habit to keep your body strong?
How many hours of sleep does a growing child need every night?

content.title: Mirror Reflection
content.description: Flex your muscles! Which healthy food did you eat today that helped build those muscles?

title: Knowledge Graph Connection
text: Healthy habits connect to what we learned about the 'Human Body'. Strong muscles need good food, and clean skin protects our body parts!

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Rainbow Plate
content.description: Draw your dinner plate tonight. Try to have at least 3 different colors of food on it (like red apples, green spinach, yellow dal). A colorful plate is a healthy plate!
